body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The shell logic `type -p curl >/dev/null || apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl` contains a precedence error. In POSIX shells, `&&` and `||` have equal precedence and are evaluated left-to-right. This means if `curl` is already present, the command evaluates as `(true || update) && install`, which attempts to run `apt-get install` without a preceding `update`. This can lead to installation failures if the package cache is stale.

Additionally, it is a Docker best practice to use `--no-install-recommends` to minimize image size and to include `ca-certificates` to ensure `curl` can properly verify HTTPS certificates during the GPG key download.

```
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    && curl -fsSL https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg | tee /usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg > /dev/null \
    && chmod go+r /usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
    && echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg] https://cli.github.com/packages stable main" | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-cli.list > /dev/null \
    && apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    gh \
    jq \
    python3 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`What is the official GitHub Actions security guidance on pinning actions to full-length commit SHAs, and what is the current commit SHA for actions/checkout v6?`

💡 Result:

GitHub officially recommends pinning actions to a full-length commit SHA as the primary method to ensure security and immutability [1]. This practice mitigates risks associated with tag manipulation—where a bad actor could alter a tag to point to malicious code—or repository compromise [1][2]. Because pinning to a tag (e.g., `@v6`) relies on a reference that can be moved or deleted, it is considered less secure than pinning to an immutable commit SHA [1][3]. Many organizations now enforce this via repository or organization-level policies, which fail workflows that use mutable tag references [1][4]. As of May 20, 2026, the current version of the actions/checkout action is v6.0.2 [5][6]. The full-length commit SHA for the v6.0.2 tag is: 44c2b7a8a4ea602854374358509873f848982cf0 [7] Note: You can always verify the SHA for any tag by running `git ls-remote https://github.com/actions/checkout v6.0.2` in your local environment, or by navigating to the "Tags" section of the repository on GitHub and clicking on the specific tag to view its corresponding commit [8][9][5].

Citations:

- 1: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use
- 2: https://gbhackers.com/compromised-github-action/
- 3: https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/pinning-github-actions-for-enhanced-security-a-complete-guide
- 4: https://www.romainlespinasse.dev/posts/github-actions-commit-sha-pinning/
- 5: https://github.com/actions/checkout/tags
